description: Composite Materials explores materials made by combining fibers and resins: how they compare with wood and metals, how they are made, two hands-on projects, and careers or hobbies that use them.

safety.note: Resins and fibers can be hazardous: work under qualified adult supervision, outdoors or with good ventilation, using the precautions on each safety data sheet.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. The 2026 update changed requirement 6 to a careers-or-hobby choice.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Likely hazards, protective equipment, handling and disposing of resins, and safety data sheets.

requirements.title: What composites are
requirements.summary: What composite materials are and how they compare with wood and metals.

requirements.title: Materials and manufacturing
requirements.summary: How composites are made, and several reinforcement materials and resins with their uses.

requirements.title: Outside research
requirements.summary: One option: visiting a company that makes or repairs composites, or reviewing composites websites.

requirements.title: Composite projects
requirements.summary: Two projects using composite materials, at least one from the pamphlet.

requirements.title: Careers or hobbies
requirements.summary: One option: a career related to composites, or a hobby that uses these skills.
